items.name: GPT-6 Sol & Luna (OpenAI)
items.summary: OpenAI expanded its GPT-6 lineup on Sep 22 with two cheaper models: Sol ($2/$10 per million tokens) for coding and professional work, and Luna ($0.10/$0.50) for high-volume tasks. Both halve their GPT-5.6 counterparts' prices while inheriting GPT-6 Astra's reasoning, coding, and computer-use improvements.

items.name: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
items.summary: Anthropic released Opus 5.5 on Sep 22, calling it the strongest-performing model it has tested, topping the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at 58. It runs ~40% cheaper than Opus 5, with $4/$20 per million tokens and much cheaper cache reads, and ships with 'preserved thinking' anti-distillation defenses.

items.name: Grok 4.7 (xAI)
items.summary: xAI launched Grok 4.7 on Sep 21, a larger base model trained with a longer RL run on multi-hour tasks and native understanding of the Grok Bot harness. It hits 46.3% on CursorBench 4.0 and tops xAI's own HackerBench safety test, priced unchanged from Grok 4.6 at $2/$6 per million tokens.

items.name: Qwen Image 2.1 (Alibaba)
items.summary: Alibaba open-sourced Qwen Image 2.1 on Sep 21, a 7B text-to-image model unifying generation and editing with native transparency support. Its compact size delivers quality compared to GPT-Image-2, though it ships under a restrictive non-commercial research license rather than Apache 2.0.

items.name: Koa (Salesforce)
items.summary: Salesforce unveiled Koa at Dreamforce 2026 (Sep 15), its first-ever reasoning model, built on Nvidia's open-weight Nemotron family and post-trained for sales, marketing, and customer support. It anchors Salesforce's push to keep enterprise customers inside its ecosystem as AI agents reshape software.
